channel.title: BotsDoThat Today
channel.description: Each weekday: 3 changes in AI assistants, what they mean for you, and one job to try.

item.title: Thursday, Nov 19: Reuters: Meta staff say Muse mixed up people's conversations and showed other users' private details, like bank balances
item.description:
1. Reuters: Meta staff say Muse mixed up people's conversations and showed other users' private details, like bank balances
Internal posts seen by Reuters describe Muse surfacing orders, childcare requests and bank balances that belonged to someone else, and nudging one employee about her Signal messages she didn't think it could see. Meta says employees test different versions than the public gets; if you use Muse, review which apps and notifications it can read and don't share more than the job needs. (TechCrunch)

2. Gemini's Mac app can now click, type and work through your apps and websites for you in a background window
Describe a chore, like copying details from PDFs into a shipping form or staging resale listings from a folder of photos, and Gemini does the clicking in a separate window while you keep using your Mac. You pick which apps it can touch and approve key steps; it's rolling out in English in the US for Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers on Apple Silicon Macs (macOS 15+). (Google)

3. Superhuman (the Grammarly company) announces a nameable personal AI assistant in Go that flags what needs you and drafts in your voice
Go, which Superhuman says has over 1 million monthly users, will get a personal assistant you can name that watches your connected tools, suggests next steps and drafts replies, with you deciding what gets done; an inbox agent for Superhuman Mail and Gmail/Outlook is in beta this month. The assistant itself rolls out over the next few months, so it's a sign-up-for-early-access item for now. (Superhuman)

Job of the day: Tell your bot where you put things, then just ask it later. Every time you store, lend or move something, tell your bot in one line. Months later, ask 'where are the spare batteries?' or 'what's in bin 4?' and it answers with the room, shelf or box.

item.title: Wednesday, Nov 18: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, a faster Gemini 4 model it pitches as close to its top Carbon model on hard work
item.description:
1. Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, a faster Gemini 4 model it pitches as close to its top Carbon model on hard work
If you pay for Google AI Pro or Ultra, you can now pick Gemini 4 Neon ("Deeper analysis") in the Gemini app for long documents, spreadsheets and multi-step agent jobs, and Google says it makes things up less often than its earlier models. Developers pay $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens with no free tier, which works out cheaper than Carbon once Carbon's promo price ends on Nov 30. (Google)

2. Grok Bot can now search and book flights, hotels and rental cars for you in one chat
Tell your Grok Bot where and when you're going and it compares fares, rooms and cars, showing bag, change and refund rules, maps and reviews, and books the option you pick. Some airlines, such as United, don't let AI agents finish a booking, and when the Bot can't confirm a final purchase it sends you the link instead, so check the details before you tap Book. (Grok Bot on X)

3. Canadians can now plan meals, fill a grocery basket and check out with Loblaw stores inside Meta's Muse
Loblaw is the first Canadian retailer connected to Muse, so you can ask your Muse for a week of meals and it builds the basket at participating Loblaw banners, remembering brands and food allergies for next time. Muse voice chats and Spaces (custom planners you describe) also reach Canada, and Muse asks before sensitive steps like a purchase. (Meta)

Job of the day: Get your car booked in for a service by letting an AI call the nearby shops. Tell your AI assistant your car is due for a service and when you're free. It phones the nearest shops or dealerships at the same time, sits on hold for you, finds one that takes appointments at a time that fits, and puts it on your calendar.

item.title: Tuesday, Nov 17: Google makes Tasks in Gemini (formerly Spark) free, so Gemini can make calls, pay and book things for you
item.description:
1. Google makes Tasks in Gemini (formerly Spark) free, so Gemini can make calls, pay and book things for you
Flip the Gemini app's toggle from Chat to Task and it works on a to-do for you, free in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India, running on the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. In the US it can also call businesses to compare quotes, buy with Google Pay after you approve, sign in with Google Password Manager, and take jobs you forward to gemini@google.com or text it; it stops and asks before purchases, and calling isn't available in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana or Nebraska. (Google)

2. OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, smarter models that use fewer words to get work done
GPT-6.2 Astra is OpenAI's new top model for hard projects like documents, spreadsheets and code, and GPT-6.2 Sol is the faster everyday model that OpenAI says beats the older GPT-6 Astra on everyday life tasks at about a seventh of the cost. Both are in ChatGPT for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users and in the API; Astra's API price drops 20% to $8 in / $40 out per million tokens, while Sol keeps $2 / $10, so bots you build on them should get cheaper per job. (OpenAI)

3. SpaceXSI says five Grok Bots now run whole accounting jobs, from invoices to collections
Each Bot owns one job (setting up accounts, billing, billing questions, matching payments, collections), learns it from a written manual over about three weeks (watch, then propose with a person approving, then work alone), and needs a person's OK for refunds and credits. SpaceXSI says invoices now go out in minutes instead of about a day; it's the company's own account, but the recipe of one clear job, written instructions and approval for money moves is a good template for any bot you set up. (SpaceXSI)

Job of the day: Get a morning check-in from your fitness watch that says how you slept and what to train today. Connect your Garmin (or Oura, Strava or Withings) data to an AI assistant and it reads your sleep, heart-rate variability (HRV), recent runs and training load, then gives you a short morning note: how recovered you look, how last week went, and a suggested session for today. Some connectors can also put an approved workout straight onto your watch.

item.title: Monday, Nov 16: Alibaba fully releases Qwen4-Max, its top model, at about a quarter of the price of the big US flagships
item.description:
1. Alibaba fully releases Qwen4-Max, its top model, at about a quarter of the price of the big US flagships
The preview from last week is now a regular paid model: $1.50 per million tokens in and $4.50 per million out on QwenCloud, 25% cheaper than Qwen3.8-Max, with a 1-million-token memory, image and video reading and tool use. It's mostly for people building their own bots who want a cheaper engine for coding and office tasks; Alibaba's claim of ~60% lower cost per task comes from its own test, so your savings may differ. (Alibaba Cloud)

2. OpenAI starts a science blog with a physicist explaining how GPT-6 Astra helped him attack a 50-year-old physics problem
It's a sign of how far the top models have come: a UC Santa Barbara physicist says GPT-6 Astra took the lead on the detailed proof behind a candidate way to define the Standard Model on a grid, with human experts checking it. He calls the result a candidate that still needs expert review, so it's a research milestone, not a new feature in ChatGPT. (OpenAI)

3. Tencent releases Hy4 flash, a very cheap model aimed at everyday office tasks
Hy4 flash costs about $0.07 per million tokens in and $0.28 out, a small fraction of most big-name models, and handles documents, research, slide decks and simple computer use with a 1-million-token memory. It's mainly for people who build their own bots and want a cheap engine for routine jobs; Tencent's claim that it matches Claude Haiku 5.5 comes from its own blind tests, and it's free in Tencent's WorkBuddy app through Nov 30. (Tencent)

Job of the day: Turn scattered booking emails into one trip sheet that flags clashes. Your flight, hotel, train and dinner confirmations are spread over five emails. Put them in one folder (or forward them) and an AI agent reads them all, writes one day-by-day trip sheet with every time, address and confirmation code, and warns you about clashes, like a flight that lands after the hotel desk closes.

item.title: Friday, Nov 13: ChatGPT Wallet lets your ChatGPT agent (a "dot") buy things for you after you approve each purchase
item.description:
1. ChatGPT Wallet lets your ChatGPT agent (a "dot") buy things for you after you approve each purchase
You add a card once, and when your dot is ready to check out you see the items, total and card, then approve with Face ID or a fingerprint; the store gets a stand-in card number, not your real one, and you keep your card's rewards and dispute protections. It's rolling out only to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers (18+) with US cards for now, and some shops may still block or decline agent purchases. (OpenAI)

2. A new standard called Poppy lets personal AI agents like Meta's Muse deal directly with stores, banks and airlines
Poppy 1.0 gives your agent an official way in to a company's site, so it can see what it's allowed to do instead of clicking around like a person: it's now on for every Muse user, every Shopify store publishes it automatically, and Mercury, Turkish Airlines and Synchrony are live. You sign in with the company to control what your agent can do, and it must ask you before certain actions like paying. (Sierra blog)

3. Anthropic invites everyone on the US Claude Duet waitlist, its always-on personal agent
If you joined the waitlist on a US Pro, Max or Ultra plan, you should now have an invite to Claude Duet, which checks your email and calendar, sends a morning brief and asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes anything. Its background checks count against your plan's limits, so Anthropic is adding free limit resets during the preview (three on Pro, one on Max and Ultra) that expire December 15. (Claude Help Center)

Job of the day: Share a scam-check bot your parent can text before they send money. Set up one AI bot with clear scam-checking instructions and share it with an older parent. When a scary call, text or email arrives ('your grandson is in jail'), they text the bot first and get a calm, plain answer and the safe next step, like calling the relative back on a saved number.

item.title: Thursday, Nov 12: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast Gemini 4 model for everyone, including free users
item.description:
1. Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast Gemini 4 model for everyone, including free users
Your Gemini app, Google Search and Gemini in Sheets now get a quicker Gemini 4 model that Google says follows instructions more closely and picks the right tools more often, so everyday tasks like email drafts, comparisons and Gmail or Drive lookups need less back-and-forth. Free Gemini users get it through auto model selection; developers pay $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with a free tier in the Gemini API. (Google blog)

2. ChatGPT's dots now follow your own instructions, like 'show me a draft before sending any emails'
You can now tell your ChatGPT dot how to behave and which actions need your go-ahead, for example always asking before it sends an email, and it keeps following that. OpenAI also says dots reply faster with less jargon; set it in the chat or under Customize, then Behavior. (ChatGPT What's new)

3. Claude can now join your Google Meet calls to take notes and build docs and whiteboards while you talk
If your workplace pays for Claude Team or Enterprise, you can add Claude to a Google Meet call and it writes the notes and action items, answers questions in the chat, and drafts docs or whiteboards that everyone on the call can edit. It's a beta for Google Meet only for now, notes and answers are free during the beta, and you should check that everyone on the call is fine with being transcribed. (Claude blog)

Job of the day: Back up your AI agent so you never lose its memory (and move it to a new computer). If your agent runs on your own computer or server, its memory, chats, automations and logins live in a folder that one crash could wipe. OpenClaw has a built-in backup and restore, and one user just moved 9 agents and 800+ sessions to a bigger server with 11 minutes of downtime.

item.title: Wednesday, Nov 11: Grok Bot can now join your Google Meet, Zoom or Teams call, answer questions in the chat and send a summary after
item.description:
1. Grok Bot can now join your Google Meet, Zoom or Teams call, answer questions in the chat and send a summary after
Paste a meeting link into your Bot's chat and ask it to join; the host lets it in, and it keeps track of decisions, answers questions in the meeting chat and sends notes and action items afterward. It's for Team, Enterprise and Ultra plans, and you should tell everyone on the call that a bot is listening. (Grok Bot changelog)

2. Alibaba says Qwen4 is coming and opens a two-week preview of its top model, Qwen4-Max
Qwen4-Max is Alibaba's new flagship for coding, office work and agent tasks, and it can read images and video, search the web and use tools with a 1-million-token memory. For now it's only a preview through Alibaba's Token Plan subscription and a few of its own apps (Qwen app, QwenWork, Qoder, QwenStudio); the preview runs until Nov 25 and there's no pay-as-you-go price yet. (Alibaba Cloud)

3. Google's new Gemini Decision 1 model answers up to 1,000 yes/no or pick-one questions in a fraction of a second
Instead of writing a reply, it scores fixed choices (is this email urgent, which tool should the bot use, does this photo break a rule) and returns how confident it is in about 150-250 milliseconds. It's a developer tool in Google AI Studio at $0.10 per million input tokens with nothing charged for output, so bot builders can make cheap, fast sorting and routing steps without paying a big model to think. (Google blog)

Job of the day: Let AI agents dig through public data on a hobby question (and try to prove you wrong). Two non-scientists just used teams of AI agents on free public data: one found a Maya ruin hidden under jungle in NASA lidar scans overnight, the other turned up two planet candidates that NASA's TESS team has now listed. You pick the question and the rules; the agents do the hours of looking, checking and writing up.

item.title: Tuesday, Nov 10: Google's top model, Gemini 4 Carbon, is now open to paying developers and Google AI Ultra subscribers
item.description:
1. Google's top model, Gemini 4 Carbon, is now open to paying developers and Google AI Ultra subscribers
Carbon is Google's strongest model for long, multi-step jobs like big coding projects, research and security work, and it's now in the Gemini API for every paying developer at $2 in / $10 out per million tokens until Nov 30 ($4 / $20 from Dec 1), plus the Gemini app, AI Mode and Antigravity for Ultra subscribers. It uses more tokens than Gemini 4 Argon to think things through, so Google still points most everyday work to Argon; Antigravity also gets a /swarm preview that turns one prompt into a team of agents. (Google blog)

2. Meta's Muse now has its own email address, so you can forward it emails to handle
Paid Muse subscribers in the US and Canada can copy Muse on a thread or forward it a message, and it will send the replies and follow-ups for you. Because it writes on your behalf, start with low-stakes emails and check what it sends before trusting it with clients or money. (The Verge)

3. eBay appears to be blocking AI agents like Meta's Muse from browsing its listings
If your bot used to pull eBay deals into a daily digest, it may now come back empty or send you to copycat sites; eBay says it restricts agent access in some cases and already banned agents that buy without a person reviewing the order. Amazon also blocks outside agents, so check the store's own app or alerts when your bot hits a wall. (The Verge)

Job of the day: Hand your agent a quick errand from your smartwatch. Meta's Muse agent now has an Apple Watch and Wear OS app. Say or type a quick errand on your wrist, like finding movie tickets or fixing a calendar clash, and approve the result without pulling out your phone.

item.title: Monday, Nov 9: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2, its top model, 20% cheaper and up to 30% faster
item.description:
1. Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2, its top model, 20% cheaper and up to 30% faster
Claude's most capable generally available model gets better at coding, reasoning and vision, and is built to run long projects and teams of agents. It's out today on all platforms at $8 / $40 per million tokens (down from $10 / $50), eligible paid Claude plans get extra Fable usage this week, and the cyber- and biology-unlocked twin, Mythos 5.2, stays limited to vetted organizations. (Anthropic)

2. ChatGPT dots can now use more than one of your computers and you pick which one per task
Connect each computer from the ChatGPT desktop app on it, then tell your dot which machine a task should run on, for example building and testing on a spare desktop while you keep working on your laptop. Each computer needs the ChatGPT app open and online, and you can revoke access per machine. (ChatGPT Learn)

3. Meta's new Muse Ember is a tiny, very cheap model built for the busywork agents repeat all day
At $0.10 in / $0.50 out per million tokens, Ember is meant for tool calls, quick coding fixes, sorting and reading long documents, and Meta says it matches Claude Haiku 5.5 at about a third of the cost per task. It's on the Meta Model API and Muse Code now, with a 1M-token context window, so cheap helper bots can run far more steps for pennies. (Meta AI)

Job of the day: Teach your bot to remember what works, so it stops repeating mistakes. A bot that forgets everything between chats makes the same mistake twice. Give it a notes file it reads at the start and updates at the end, and it gets better every week. Anthropic published how it does this for Claude.

item.title: Friday, Nov 6: Meta brings Muse Wonder-style memory and focus to Muse and Meta AI
item.description:
1. Meta brings Muse Wonder-style memory and focus to Muse and Meta AI
Muse and Meta AI get specialized models trained with Muse Wonder so they remember what still matters across chats (Active Memory) and keep pushing when a task hits a snag (Active Focus). Meta says Muse forgets critical goal details 2.4x less often and finishes everyday tasks with surprises 67% more often; Meta AI should ask sharper follow-ups and handle mid-chat course changes better. (Meta AI Research)

2. Meta's Muse can now build you a custom 'space' like a planner, tracker or game
Describe what you want (a gift tracker, wedding planner, school-events dashboard or trip planner) and Muse builds it as a space inside the app that you can pin to your tabs and keep editing. If you connect apps like Gmail, Calendar or OpenTable, a space updates itself in the background; it's available everywhere Muse is. (Meta Newsroom)

3. Anthropic explains how 'dreaming' helps Claude fix and organize its memory between sessions
Anthropic shows how Claude can go back over its own past work while idle to correct wrong notes, merge duplicates and build a wiki of what it knows, so a long-running agent repeats fewer mistakes. It's an engineering explainer, not a new button, but it's a good model for any bot you run: have it review and tidy its notes regularly. (Anthropic)

Job of the day: Ask Claude about your own spending across your banks. Claude's Personal Finance beta lets you link US bank and card accounts through Plaid, then ask plain questions like "where did my money go last month?" It can only read your accounts — it can't move, manage or invest your money.

item.title: Thursday, Nov 5: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a security model that finds and helps fix software bugs
item.description:
1. OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a security model that finds and helps fix software bugs
Approved security teams can use GPT-6 Cyber to hunt for real software holes, check they work, and draft fixes, with stronger rules to stay inside the job they were given. It's only for Daybreak Red customers for now (not everyday ChatGPT), and OpenAI says it already helped find hundreds of Linux and Firefox issues. (OpenAI)

2. Muse gets real-time voice chat and expressive avatars in the US
In the Muse app on mobile, web and Mac in the US, tap the phone icon to talk out loud while your Muse's avatar reacts with expressions and gestures, and pick from hundreds of voices. Meta says it's useful for thinking through a trip or rehearsing an interview hands-free, with AI Glasses and Muse Charm support coming later. (Meta)

3. Claude can now read your bank and card accounts and answer money questions (US beta)
On Pro, Max and Ultra in the US, connect selected bank, card, loan or investment accounts through Plaid and ask Claude where your money went, what's due before payday, or whether a trip fits the budget. Access is read-only so Claude can't move or invest money, chats in the Personal Finance hub aren't used for training, and Anthropic says it isn't designed to give investment advice. (Claude (Anthropic))

Job of the day: Have an AI agent research your family history for you. MyHeritage just launched GAIA, an AI research agent that takes a question like 'who were my great-grandfather's parents?', searches old records and your family tree on its own, and shows you what it found with a confidence rating. Nothing goes into your tree until you approve it.

item.title: Wednesday, Nov 4: Grok Bot can now phone businesses for you, like cancelling a plan or booking an appointment
item.description:
1. Grok Bot can now phone businesses for you, like cancelling a plan or booking an appointment
Tell Grok Bot who to call and why, approve the call, and it waits on hold, works the phone menu and talks to the agent while you watch a live transcript and can take over at any time, then it sends you a summary. It only calls U.S. numbers for now (not Washington or Illinois), says up front that it's a virtual assistant, and some reps may refuse to deal with an AI. (TeslaNorth)

2. ChatGPT Images 2.6 can make animated GIFs and remember a saved reference photo
Ask ChatGPT for a looping GIF or to animate a still photo, and save a photo (say, of your dog) under a name so you can reuse it later by typing @ and that name. It's on all ChatGPT plans and in Codex, about 50% faster than before, with GIFs rolling out gradually; ChatGPT can't edit an animated GIF you upload. (OpenAI Help Center)

3. OpenAI's AI agents found and drafted patches for 948 Linux 'get root' security holes
In one mid-October test, OpenAI's autonomous security pipeline checked the Linux kernel, proved 948 ways a normal user could become admin, and wrote candidate patches for human review, at about $1.2 million in API cost. Humans still review and report the fixes; the run used an upcoming cyber model that became GPT-6 Cyber. (OpenAI)

Job of the day: Stop your AI chats from being used for training (and check it stays off). Paying for ChatGPT or Gemini doesn't automatically keep your chats out of model training. This week Hacker News users found Gemini keeps training on saved chats unless you turn off Keep Activity, and some ChatGPT users said the Codex training switch had turned itself back on. Here's how to switch it off and re-check it.

item.title: Tuesday, Nov 3: OpenAI shows ChatGPT and Codex designing physical products, including a small device built with almost no human edits
item.description:
1. OpenAI shows ChatGPT and Codex designing physical products, including a small device built with almost no human edits
OpenAI says its models now help engineers with CAD drawings, circuit boards and simulations, and two staff used GPT-6 Astra to design a small Codex talk-to device that a factory then built in under a month. It's a progress report and a call for engineering partners, not a new product you can buy, and OpenAI admits the model still missed manufacturing limits that humans had to fix. (OpenAI)

2. Anthropic open-sources FlashProve, a way to mathematically prove which AI model wrote a reply
FlashProve lets an AI company publish a fingerprint of its model and then attach a proof to each answer showing that exact model produced it, so you could check you're not being quietly served a cheaper model. It's an early research prototype (tested on Meta's open Llama 4 Maverick, short 1,024-token requests only), and Anthropic hasn't said it will offer proofs for Claude. (Anthropic)

3. Netflix tests an AI Discover tab that picks something to watch based on your mood
Pick a theme like "something light", "scare me" or "quick watches" and Netflix's AI suggests titles, and you can tell it to stop showing ones you don't want. It's rolling out first to English-language US members on supported TVs, as an experiment Netflix may change. (TechCrunch)

Job of the day: Keep a visa application on track with an AI agent. Tell an agent "get my visa by the end of November" and it lists what you need, tracks missing documents and reminds you until it's done. It can also spot an upcoming trip in your calendar and flag visa rules and arrival forms.

item.title: Monday, Nov 2: xAI shows Data Bot, a shared Grok Bot that answers any employee's data questions like a data scientist
item.description:
1. xAI shows Data Bot, a shared Grok Bot that answers any employee's data questions like a data scientist
xAI's data team taught a shared Team Bot their metrics, experiment rules and chart styles, so anyone can ask it in chat or Slack to dig into numbers or build a dashboard. xAI estimates it did about 70 hours of the data team's work in one week (its own figure), and it's a how-we-use-it example you can copy with Team Bots, not a separate product. (xAI)

2. New GDPx test finds even the best AI agent finishes only 12% of real expert work tasks
A useful reality check before handing an agent serious professional work: across 206 long tasks in 11 fields, Claude Opus 5.5 scored 12.0%, Gemini 4 Carbon 10.9% and GPT-6 Astra 9.6%, and every model scored zero on the finance and legal tasks under pass/fail grading. SemiAnalysis says it will refresh the leaderboard every three to six months. (SemiAnalysis)

3. Claude's API can now remember the conversation for you, making long agent sessions about a third faster to answer
If you use Claude-powered agents or coding tools, long sessions should start replying faster: with the new message threads beta the server keeps the conversation, so the app only sends new messages, and Anthropic says the median wait for the first word drops about 35% on very long (500k to 1M token) chats. Price and token use stay the same, and a thread expires five minutes after its last request. (Claude Platform release notes)

Job of the day: Make your agent prove it really booked, sent or saved it. Agents sometimes say "all set!" when the booking, update or message never went through. A new test of 19 AI models found this was the most common way they broke the rules. The fix is simple: ask your agent to show proof (a confirmation number, a link, a screenshot or the confirmation email) and to check the real result before it tells you it's done.

item.title: Friday, Oct 30: Claude renames Max 20x to Ultra and drops the five-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts
item.description:
1. Claude renames Max 20x to Ultra and drops the five-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts
At the same $200 a month, verified Ultra subscribers can now use their whole week's allowance whenever they like instead of hitting a reset every five hours; the weekly limit itself didn't change. The $100 Max 5x plan is now just called Max, and you don't need to do anything if you subscribe. (Claude Help Center)

2. Reality check: DoorDash has seen only 'several hundred' orders from outside AI shopping agents
Agents like Meta's Muse can order food for you, but almost nobody is doing it yet: DoorDash counts a few hundred agent orders against millions of normal ones, and Amazon's CEO called outside shopping agents 'still not great.' For now, your bot works best for finding and comparing; expect to finish checkout yourself on many stores. (TechCrunch)

3. ChatGPT tightens weapons answers for teens and can end chats fixated on violence
If a teen in your house uses ChatGPT, it will now refuse more weapons details, and for everyone it limits step-by-step recreations of past mass attacks. It can also end conversations stuck on violence and may briefly pause an account, and OpenAI says it will publish its first community safety report in early 2027. (OpenAI)

Job of the day: Have your bot catch calendar clashes hiding in your email. Plans don't only live in your calendar. A rescheduled event in a confirmation email, or a "call Mom at 2" note you emailed yourself, can quietly clash with what's booked. An always-on agent can compare your email with your calendar every morning and text you before a clash, but in WIRED's test of six agents only two caught one on their own, so ask for this check by name.

item.title: Thursday, Oct 29: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro's Work and Codex limits and cancels the planned Pro 200 cut
item.description:
1. OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro's Work and Codex limits and cancels the planned Pro 200 cut
Same price, more agent time: Pro 100 and Pro 500 now get twice their previous Work and Codex allowance, Business Premium gets more too, and the Pro 200 reduction announced in September is off. It applies automatically from Oct 29, and usage by your dot still counts separately. (ChatGPT release notes)

2. Gemini can now make and edit documents, PDFs, slides and spreadsheets right in the chat
Ask Gemini for a file, like a PDF study guide from photos of your handwritten notes, then type your own edits or highlight a part and ask Gemini to change it. It's free for all users; PDFs work on web and mobile, other formats on the web only. (Google blog)

3. Pika releases H3 Flex, a fast video-with-sound model with open weights
It makes a 15-second clip with a soundtrack in seconds, can follow up to 12 reference images, videos or voice clips, and upscales your favorite to 4K. It's on the Pika API now and comes to the Pika app on Nov 2; the downloadable weights' license excludes the US, EU, UK and Korea. (Pika)

Job of the day: Set up an AI coach that helps you (or your teen) start overwhelming tasks and checks in. A parent shared how they set up ChatGPT as a "getting started" coach for their 20-year-old son with ADHD: one chat for schedule and check-ins, a Project for each big job so it remembers progress, and instructions to ask one question at a time and give one five-minute first step. Scheduled check-ins keep it going without anyone nagging.

item.title: Wednesday, Oct 28: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its new top model, but only a few security teams can use it so far
item.description:
1. Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its new top model, but only a few security teams can use it so far
Carbon is Google's strongest model yet: it now ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and is built for long coding jobs and for finding and fixing security holes. This week only selected cyber defenders get it; Google says developers, businesses and the Gemini app get it 'as soon as possible', at the same intro API price as Argon ($2 in / $10 out per million tokens, later $4 / $20). (Google blog)

2. You can now text your ChatGPT dot over iMessage or RCS
Your dot (ChatGPT's always-on agent) can now take tasks by text, photo or voice note from your phone's Messages app, and text you back when something needs you. It's a beta for US ChatGPT Pro users only, one-to-one (no group chats), and it can't see your other text conversations. (ChatGPT Learn)

3. Claude for Legal gets ready-made tools for contract review, cite checks and rule tracking
Legal teams can start from a gallery of ready-to-use Claude 'artifacts', such as a contract comparison table, a citation checker and a regulation timeline, add their own documents and share them with coworkers. Every answer links back to its source, and a lawyer still reviews the result; it's aimed at businesses and law firms, not personal legal advice. (Claude blog)

Job of the day: Add an AI to your friends' group chat to make plans happen. Instead of 60 messages about where and when, you add an AI agent to the iMessage group. It suggests options, gets everyone to agree, and then books the table, tickets or rental car for the group once someone says yes.

item.title: Tuesday, Oct 27: Meta's Muse personal agent launches in Singapore, its first country after the US
item.description:
1. Meta's Muse personal agent launches in Singapore, its first country after the US
Muse, Meta's do-it-for-you agent, now works in Singapore with local apps like Grab, Shopee and Singapore Airlines. It's free for most tasks, keeps your passwords and cards out of the agent's view, and asks before sending an email or buying anything. (Meta)

2. Grok Bot can now buy things you approve, track the order and cancel subscriptions you don't use
Grok Bot 0.78.1 shows shopping results as product cards with a Buy now button that still waits for your OK, then tracks the package. New templates start a free trial and cancel it before it bills, find unused subscriptions and watch renewal prices, and the Bot confirms with you before changing anything. (Grok Bot changelog)

3. Google DeepMind shows Genie 4, a world model you can steer like a live video game
Genie 4 builds a realistic, explorable scene from a text prompt, with sound and talking characters, and changes it in real time when you type things like 'make it rain'. It's only with trusted testers for now; Google says Google AI Ultra subscribers (in Project Genie) and early Gemini API partners come next, so there's nothing for your bots to use yet. (Google DeepMind blog)

Job of the day: Find an apartment that fits your must-have list. Tell ChatGPT your budget, area, pets and must-haves, and a rental app inside it (Apartments.com, Zumper, RentCafe or Apartment List) searches live listings, compares them side by side and can request a tour.

item.title: Monday, Oct 26: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, files to go public on Nasdaq
item.description:
1. Anthropic, the maker of Claude, files to go public on Nasdaq
Anthropic has filed the paperwork with the SEC for a stock market listing under the symbol ANT; the share count and price aren't set yet. Nothing changes in Claude for you today, but a public Anthropic will have to report its business openly, which can shape pricing and plans down the road. (Anthropic)

2. GPT-6.1 Terra: OpenAI's new fast, cheaper model for bots that use apps and screens
GPT-6.1 Terra is a new mid-size OpenAI model that's better at reading what's on a screen and clicking through apps for you, like filling out forms or entering invoices, and makes fewer factual mistakes than GPT-5.6 Terra. It's in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API at $1 in / $5 out per million tokens, half the price of GPT-6.1 Sol, so bots that do lots of computer work get cheaper to run; the benchmark claims are OpenAI's own. (OpenAI API changelog)

3. Claude gets a free plugin for nonprofits that helps with fundraising, marketing and hiring
Verified nonprofits using Claude now get a plugin, built with about 30 nonprofits, with ready-made skills for grant research, donor reports, marketing and hiring that follow the group's own policies. If you volunteer for or run a small nonprofit, it's a quicker way to get Claude doing the paperwork that eats your week. (Claude)

Job of the day: Build a small app for yourself just by describing it. Describe a little tool you wish existed, like a chore chart, a tip splitter or a packing checklist, and Claude builds a working version beside the chat. Ask for changes in plain words.

item.title: Friday, Oct 23: Block shows Dessa, a voice AI that talks with human-like pauses and emotion
item.description:
1. Block shows Dessa, a voice AI that talks with human-like pauses and emotion
Dessa is a speech model from the company behind Square and Cash App that listens and talks at the same time, so conversations with it sound strikingly like a real person. There's no public access yet, only early access for safety researchers, but it's a reminder that a lifelike voice on the phone may not be a person. (TechCrunch)

2. OpenAI cuts its newest models off the live internet while they're being trained
OpenAI says its frontier models now train in an offline copy of the web instead of the real internet, a safety step so a model in training can't reach outside systems. Nothing changes in ChatGPT for you, but it shows labs are treating stronger models as something to keep fenced in. (OpenAI)

3. Kimi K3.1 Pro: a new open model that says it nearly matches Claude Opus 5.5 at coding
Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro is in the Kimi apps and API, and its full weights are now on Hugging Face (under Moonshot's own Kimi K3.1 Pro License), though at 2.8 trillion parameters it needs data-center hardware to run. Its API price is $2 in / $10 out per million tokens, half of Claude Opus 5.5's list price; the coding scores are Moonshot's own. (The Next Web)

Job of the day: Add calendar events and reminders just by asking your bot. Instead of opening your calendar and typing everything in, you tell your phone's AI assistant "add this" or "remind me", and it puts the event or reminder in the right app. Grok Bot and Gemini can both do this now, once you allow them into those apps.
